title: Controlled KV Promotion / Prefetch Prototype

section_7_graph_rebuild_investigation.finding: No new graph-rebuild primitive is needed to CONSUME a live-rebound tensor, because llama.cpp already rebuilds the ggml graph from scratch on every single llama_decode call (confirmed by reading llama-graph.cpp: mctx_cur->get_k(ctx0, il) is called fresh inside graph construction, e.g. build_attn, at lines 2674/2765/2850/2929 of llama-graph.cpp). get_k/get_v (llama-kv-cache.cpp:1285/1305) simply return layers[ikv].k/.v (or a view of it) at whatever address that pointer currently holds.
section_7_graph_rebuild_investigation.actual_blocker: llama_kv_cache::layers (llama-kv-cache.h:297, std::vector<kv_layer>) is declared under a `private:` section (llama-kv-cache.h:232) with no public setter. It is populated exactly once via layers.push_back(...) during cache construction (llama-kv-cache.cpp:279) and never written to again anywhere in the file (confirmed by grep across all layers[...] accesses in llama-kv-cache.cpp -- every other site is a read, e.g. lines 884, 1245, 1249, 1266, 1288, 1308, 1342, 1377).
section_7_graph_rebuild_investigation.conclusion: This is NOT a graph-rebuild problem (D. GRAPH_REBUILD_REQUIRED does not apply) -- it is narrower: the graph already re-resolves layers[ikv].k/.v fresh every decode call, so simply mutating that pointer between calls would be sufficient for the next decode to pick up a new device/location automatically, with no other llama.cpp code changes.

section_25_upstream_patch_bar.insufficiency_of_phase12b_patch: Phase 12B's kv_dev_override only runs once, at llama_kv_cache construction time (inside the per-layer allocation loop) -- it has no mechanism to run again after construction, and there is no public API surface on llama_kv_cache to trigger it again or to otherwise replace layers[ikv].k/.v post-construction.
section_25_upstream_patch_bar.exact_missing_primitive: A public (or membrane-friend, matching the kv_dev_override/kv_type_override pattern already used by Phase 11/12B) method on llama_kv_cache, e.g. `bool relocate_layer(int32_t il, ggml_backend_buffer_type_t new_buft)`, that: (1) allocates a new k/v tensor pair on new_buft with the same dims/type as the existing layers[il].k/.v, (2) copies the real bytes via ggml_backend_tensor_copy (or get+set, as this phase's probe already does manually via scratch tensors), (3) rebuilds layers[il].k_stream/v_stream views against the new tensor, (4) replaces layers[il].k/.v with the new tensor, and (5) frees the old buffer. No change to get_k/get_v, llama-graph.cpp, or the scheduler is needed -- they already re-read layers[il].k/.v fresh every decode.
section_25_upstream_patch_bar.exact_source_location: third_party/llama.cpp/src/llama-kv-cache.h:232-297 (private kv_layer/layers), third_party/llama.cpp/src/llama-kv-cache.cpp:220-280 (construction loop where the current one-shot device placement happens).
section_25_upstream_patch_bar.smallest_possible_patch_scope_estimate: Roughly 40-70 added lines: one new public method plus (2)/(3)/(4)/(5) above, reusing existing helpers (ctx_for_buft, ggml_backend_tensor_copy, ggml_backend_buffer_free) already present in the file. No changes to llama-graph.cpp, the scheduler, or any public llama.h struct are required.
section_25_upstream_patch_bar.generic_upstreamable: Plausibly upstreamable in spirit (KV-cache device relocation is a generically useful capability), but NOT written or proposed as an actual patch in this phase per the Section 25 instruction to stop and report instead of patching automatically.
section_25_upstream_patch_bar.expected_maintenance_burden: Moderate: llama_kv_cache's internals (kv_layer, the allocation loop, defrag/resize logic) are actively developed upstream; a relocate_layer method touching the same private state would need to be kept in sync the same way the existing kv_dev_override/kv_type_override membrane patches already are (see patches/llama.cpp-membrane-kv-device-override.patch, patches/llama.cpp-membrane-kv-type-override.patch for the established maintenance pattern and its disclosed burden in Phase 12B's maintenance.json).
section_25_upstream_patch_bar.decision: STOPPED before writing this patch, per Section 25 instruction -- reporting findings only.

vulkan_release.result: PASS -- full experiment suite (info/promote/demote/multi_schedule/copybench/cycle/stall/prefetch) run for real against SmolLM2-135M/360M on the GTX 1650; 68/68 ctest suite passing including all pre-existing product tests

tests.sanitizer_limitation: No Vulkan+ASan/UBSan combination build was attempted this phase -- building one from scratch on this 5.6 GiB RAM host (already needed ~580s and most of available RAM for the CPU-only ASan rebuild alone) was judged too resource-risky, and Vulkan driver-side allocations are frequently not ASan-instrumented anyway (a known source of false positives/negatives for this class of combo). The real GPU byte-copy path was instead verified via: (a) real Vulkan Release runs with byte-hash round-trip verification in every promote/demote/multi_schedule/copybench trial, and (b) cycle_stability.json (50 repeated alloc/copy/free cycles) as an external (nvidia-smi + RSS), sanitizer-independent leak/corruption check.
tests.product_regression: 68/68 ctest suite passes on build-vulkan, including test_product_cli, test_adaptive_kv_policy, test_gpu_policy, test_compat_check, test_mem_guard (covering the native/q8/q5/adaptive/compare/gpu-bench/auto/guard --kv modes) -- tools/membrane-run/product_cli.cpp and every other product source file are byte-for-byte untouched this phase (git diff confirms only CMakeLists.txt, scripts/verify-results.py, and the new tools/membrane-kv-promotion-prefetch/ directory changed).

limitations: This phase does NOT achieve live KV tiering -- every promotion/demotion this phase performs is a real, correct, byte-verified COPY that the live decode graph never reads (classification B, independently re-verified against llama.cpp source, not just inferred from comments).

weight_device per-layer capture in the probe is a known instrumentation gap (always reports MISSING) -- weight GPU-residency is established indirectly via mp.n_gpu_layers=-1 and measured VRAM baselines, not per-tensor capture.
headroom_rule false-safe/false-reject audit has only 3 real data points; not a powered validation of the exact constant values.
Copy/stall/prefetch measurements are all at SmolLM2-135M/360M scale (largest real pressure test at ctx=200000/360M) on a single GTX 1650 -- not validated at larger models or multi-GPU.
No product code path, CLI, or adaptive policy was touched -- entirely research-only, matching the phase's constraints.

1 of 7 failure-case scenarios (interrupted copy mid-transfer) was not exercised as a real fault injection this phase -- no mechanism in this prototype to abort an in-flight ggml_backend_tensor_set/get call.
unresolved_issues: Whether a relocate_layer-style primitive (Section 25) would actually preserve correctness under concurrent/streaming decode (multi-sequence, batched) was not tested -- this phase used single-sequence greedy generation throughout.

Whether async prefetch overlap holds at larger KV-layer byte counts (e.g. the ctx=200000/360M pressure-regime scale, ~130 MiB/layer) was not measured -- prefetch_result.json only covers the 135M/ctx=2048 scale.
decision_gate_meaning: Copies work: real, byte-verified, precision-independent (Q8_0/Q5_1), correct at both tested model scales and at the real ctx=200000 pressure boundary. But tensor/backend placement is fixed after llama_context construction -- true live tiering requires another primitive (Section 25: a relocate_layer-style method on llama_kv_cache, not yet written).
next_step_recommendation: Design the smallest runtime rebind primitive: a llama_kv_cache::relocate_layer(il, new_buft) method (see section_25_upstream_patch_bar.exact_missing_primitive) that reassigns layers[il].k/.v after a real byte copy. Because llama.cpp already rebuilds its graph fresh every llama_decode call, no other engine change is needed for the next decode to pick up the new location -- this is a narrowly-scoped, well-localized addition, not a rearchitecture. Do NOT execute this next step in this phase.

bugs_found_and_fixed_this_phase.bug: cmd_info and cmd_move (promote/demote) read cap.k_leaf/v_leaf/w_leaf (populated only by the cb_eval callback during a real decode) BEFORE ever calling decode_prompt() -- every layer reported kv_device=MISSING in info mode, and every promote/demote call misclassified its target layer (already_gpu/already_cpu) because the tensor pointer was still NULL.
bugs_found_and_fixed_this_phase.fix: moved decode_prompt() to run immediately after load_ctx()/the layer-bounds check in both cmd_info and cmd_move, before any cap.k_leaf/v_leaf read.

bugs_found_and_fixed_this_phase.bug: Every mode using ggml_backend_dev_by_type(GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_GPU) (promote/demote/multi_schedule/copybench/cycle/stall/prefetch) passed the result straight into ggml_backend_dev_buffer_type/ggml_backend_dev_init without a NULL check -- on a build with no GPU backend registered (confirmed on build-cpu-rc1, GGML_VULKAN=OFF), this hits a bare GGML_ASSERT(device) in ggml-backend.cpp and SIGABRTs the whole process instead of failing closed.
bugs_found_and_fixed_this_phase.fix: added require_gpu_device() and called it at all 7 GPU-device-acquisition sites; verified the fix on build-cpu-rc1 (now returns a clean backend_unavailable JSON error, exit code 20) and re-verified no regression on build-vulkan afterward. This also retroactively provided real evidence for the previously-untested backend_unavailable failure case (see failure_cases.json).
